subject: goldenrod crab spider
title: This Spider Spends 25 Days Repainting Itself to Ambush Bees

scenes.text: This spider needs 25 days to get dressed for dinner.
The goldenrod crab spider. A female is under a centimetre long, and she hunts on flowers.
On white daisies she's white. On goldenrod, she slowly loads her body with yellow pigment.
Turning yellow takes ten to 25 days. Going back to white takes about six.
No web. She waits with front legs spread. A bumblebee lands, she bites, and venom drops prey far bigger than her.
Twenty-five days of dressing up, for one bite.

description:
The goldenrod crab spider (Misumena vatia) ambushes insects on flowers and can switch between white and yellow to match them.
Turning from white to yellow takes about 10 to 25 days because it must produce yellow pigment; turning back takes about six days. Females are only about 6 to 10 mm long, yet without a web they grab and envenom bees and butterflies much larger than themselves.
Would you spot her on a flower?
first_comment: She can catch bumblebees many times her size without a web. What is the sneakiest hunter you know?
